site.name: github-404
site.summary: github-404-clone Clone of the GitHub 404 error page. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | 404 page: top GitHub nav bar, centered error message ("This is not the web page you are looking for."), Octocat illustration, links to home / search / contact support | | `style.css` | Dark background, illustration styling, buttons | | `app.js` | Illustration hover / parallax effect, (optional) fake search suggestions |

run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the GitHub 404 error page, focusing on interactive recovery paths, visual feedback, and mobile responsiveness.
run_plan.summary: The exploration will focus entirely on the single index.html page, validating the search input, category filters, and navigation links. It will assess the parallax effect on the Octocat illustration and verify the behavior of all interactive elements. Finally, it will repeat critical checks on a mobile viewport to evaluate the numerous small tap target warnings identified in the prescan.
assumptions: Links with href '#' are intentionally non-functional in this clone but should still be clicked to check for unexpected errors or missing feedback.
The app.js parallax effect is tied to mouse movement over the illustration area.
The search input and category buttons (Code, Repositories, People) may trigger fake search suggestions or UI changes handled by app.js.
risk_hotspots: Empty interactive label on the logo link (ux-1)
Small tap targets on footer links (contact support, GitHub Status) and category buttons (Code, Repositories, People)
Search input and button interaction flow (lack of form tag might affect expected behaviors)

phases.title: Header Navigation Validation
phases.objective: Validate the accessibility and behavior of the top navigation bar controls.
key_checks: Click the logo link (ux-1) and verify behavior, noting the empty accessible label
Click the 'Search', 'Support', and 'Status' nav links and check for any visual feedback or console errors
exit_criteria: All header links have been clicked
Accessibility issue with the logo link is documented

phases.title: Search and Recovery Flow
phases.objective: Test the primary user recovery flow via the search input and category filters.
key_checks: Type a query into the 'Search GitHub' input (ux-5) and observe if fake suggestions appear
Click the 'Search' button (ux-6) to submit the query and check for UI response
Click the 'Code', 'Repositories', and 'People' filter buttons (ux-7, ux-8, ux-9) and verify state changes or visual feedback
exit_criteria: Search input has been typed into and submitted
All three category filter buttons have been interacted with

phases.title: Illustration and Footer Interaction
phases.objective: Validate the visual parallax effect and footer link behaviors.
key_checks: Hover/move mouse over the Octocat illustration area to trigger the parallax effect
Click the 'contact support' link (ux-10) and check for feedback
Click the 'GitHub Status' link (ux-11) and check for feedback
exit_criteria: Parallax effect is confirmed working or not working
Footer links have been clicked and behaviors observed

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Checks
phases.objective: Evaluate layout shifts, tap target usability, and parallax behavior on a mobile viewport.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and check for layout overlapping or broken styling
Verify if small tap targets (especially footer links and category buttons) are usable or severely impacted
Test touch interactions on the illustration for the parallax effect
exit_criteria: Mobile layout has been screenshot and assessed
Tap target severity has been validated via interaction

coverage_targets.features: 100% of visible controls (11 interactables) and the parallax visual effect
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat all critical interactions and layout checks on mobile viewport

notes: Pay special attention to the lack of a <form> element around the search input and button, which might affect standard submit behaviors.
Document whether the small tap targets identified in the prescan actually hinder interaction on the mobile viewport.
